title: Behavior-drift profiles and weighted sampling on version locks
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Summary:
We will introduce a two-tiered automated evaluation mechanism that triggers during catalog or tenant model version locks. Rather than always running full sample suites, this ticket designs 'behavior-drift profiles' that characterize how a model’s outputs change along important axes (semantic intent, safety tags, token-length distribution, hallucination rate). Using those profiles we compute a lightweight predicted drift score for an upgrade, and schedule a weighted-sampling eval that balances cost and coverage across tenants.

Problem:
Current preflight and post-pin evals either run a standard full sample set (expensive) or a naive random sample (misses low-volume tenants and semantic edge cases). This leads to missed regressions for low-traffic customers and unnecessary cost for catalog-wide upgrades.

Goals:
- Define behavior-drift profiles per model family that map to eval heuristics (e.g., which metrics matter most).
- Implement a weighted sampling engine that picks tenant and catalog samples by a combination of recent traffic, diversity score, and risk weight (SLA/custom features).
- Add a fast predictive estimator that uses delta-features to decide if a full fidelity run is required.
- Integrate with pin event pipeline to trigger shadow evaluations, surface early warnings in Console, and create auto rollback suggestions for high-risk changes.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change rollout mechanics (canaries/traffic splits) or implement automated rollback without human approval.

Success metrics:
- Detect regressions that otherwise would have been missed for tenants representing at least 10% of customer incidents during model upgrades in first month of rollout.
- Reduce catalog-level full-run evals by 35% for minor config tweaks while keeping regression detection rate >= current baseline.
- Mean time from pin event to first alert < 20 minutes for catalog pins, < 10 minutes for customer-pinned critical tenants.

Acceptance criteria:
- Behavior-drift profile schema defined and stored in catalog metadata.
- Weighted sampling service implemented and registered as an eval trigger option in the pin orchestration layer.
- Dashboard panels added to Console showing drift score, sampling rationale, and sampled tenants for every pin event.
- A/B test run with 100 catalog pins showing cost savings and no increase in undetected regression incidents (comparative analysis).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Drift profile schema (versioned) in catalog metadata repository. 2) Sampling service accepts parameters: window_days, risk_weight, diversity_target and returns sample list. 3) Pin event flow calls sampling service and either (a) fires full eval or (b) schedules progressive fidelity runs depending on predicted drift. 4) Console shows a per-pin report with: predicted drift score, sample coverage, metrics delta, and link to full eval logs. 5) Runbook for triage created and reviewed by SRE/QA.
runbook: If predictive estimator returns drift_score > 0.6: 1) UI shows red alert and opens priority eval job; 2) Notify on #evals-ops and assigned oncall; 3) Follow triage steps in CONFLUENCE: https://confluence.company/pm/91288-triage; 4) If regression confirmed, follow rollback playbook and create incident ticket pointing to pin event ID and sampled cases.
comments: 2026-03-05 Aisha Menon: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded; design sketch attached. Primary constraint is keeping cost delta under 25% of current eval spend. Link: https://drive.company/designs/pm-91288/kickoff

2026-03-07 Marco Nguyen: Engineering feasibility review — ENG proposes a lightweight estimator using cached metric deltas and a small transformer classifier trained on historical pin outcomes. Concern: training labels are noisy. Action: run label cleanup job (ENG-42177).

2026-03-09 Priya Shah (Data Science): Proposed behavior axes: semantic-shift, verbosity, safety-flag-rate, hallucination-susceptibility. Submitted sample mapping and scoring functions in Confluence. Link: https://confluence.company/ds/behavior-profiles
2026-03-10 Design review (Luca): UI should make sampling rationale human-readable; suggested cards: 'Why we sampled this tenant' and 'What we expect to change'. Requested copy for Console.

2026-03-11 ENG PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-orchestrator/pull/234 — includes sampling engine and estimator prototype. Tests: unit + small integration harness. Waiting on feedback from QA.

2026-03-12 Security review note: sampling may surface PII in exemplar payloads. Decision: apply tokenization/hash transform for tenant samples and run privacy-preserving mode by default for regulated customers. See security doc: https://drive.company/security/pin-sampling-privacy.pdf

2026-03-13 PM review: Trade-offs accepted — prioritization: 1) tenant safety 2) detection recall 3) cost. Requested rollout plan: start with 20% of catalog pins and 100% of high-risk customer-pinned events.

2026-03-14 QA: Integration run results attached — estimator flagged 18% of catalog upgrades as high drift; weighted-sampling test captured 92% of regression signals found in full-run baseline on the A/B cohort. Link to dashboard: https://dash.company/evals/pm-91288-abtest
